newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian PM fights to prevent government collapse.
newsitem.headline: Estonian PM fights to prevent government collapse.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi fought on Wednesday to defuse a row with his coalition partners and prevent the government from collapsing.
The coalition, the sixth since Estonia quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, came under threat after Vaehi's Coalition Party agreed to cooperate with the leading opposition group, the Centre Party.
The agreement was a huge slap in the face for the Reform Party, the junior coalition partner, which gave Vaehi until Wednesday afternoon to scrap the deal.
The Reformists are expected to decide whether to quit the one-year-old government at a meeting on Thursday .
Vaehi has refused to cancel the pact with the Centre Party and has tried to reassure his partners that the deal would not lead to the Centre Party joining the coalition.

"If the Reform Party sticks to its position that new members, in this case the Centre Party, are not to be included in the governing coalition, then the Coalition Party will agree to this," the prime minister told a news conference.
He said his party would send a letter to the Reformists by the Wednesday deadline to explain its position.
The Reformists were angered by a clause in the cooperation deal, which said Vaehi's party would work to include the Centre Party in the coalition.
Vaehi insisted the wording meant only that the Coalition and Centre parties would work together to "strengthen democracy".
The previous government was a Coalition/Centre partnership which collapsed amid scandal after the Centre Party leader was found to have taped confidential conversations.
Estonia, deemed one of the most successful reformers in eastern Europe, has managed to keep on a steady path of reform despite frequent political turmoil.
